title: The Curve and Morpho Integration Boost Instances name an identical reward address
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.2.1.2 gives the Curve reward address as `0xa7843f843d29ca33ba48d9d1335b774eecc328dc`. A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.3.1.2 gives the Morpho reward address as the same string. The two Base-chain Instances, Euler and Compound, each have distinct addresses.

Two readings are possible, and the Artifact does not disambiguate. Either the field names a Sky-side distribution contract that fans rewards out to Mainnet integrations — in which case the label "Integration Partner Reward Address" is misleading, since it is not the partner's address — or it is a copy-paste error in a `[Core]` parameter that determines where money goes.

Either way it complicates a reader's ability to audit payments per partner. The Payment Details schema used in the Distribution Reward primitive ties each payment to a Payment Address, which only distinguishes payees if addresses are unique per payee. Two Instances sharing an address means on-chain transfers to it cannot be attributed to Curve versus Morpho from the Artifact alone.

The pattern — distinct addresses on Base, one shared address on Mainnet — is at least suggestive of a routing contract rather than an error, since a mistake would be unlikely to respect the chain boundary so cleanly. But that is inference, not something the document states, which is itself the finding: a parameter this load-bearing should not require inference.
description: Both record `0xa7843f843d29ca33ba48d9d1335b774eecc328dc`, so on Mainnet the Integration Partner Reward Address designates a shared payment route rather than a partner-controlled wallet.
